title.zh: 卷386 列傳一百七十三 文庆 文祥 宝鋆
title.en: Volume 386 Biographies 173: Wen Qing, Wen Xiang, Bao Yun
title.raw: 卷386 列傳一百七十三 文庆 文祥 宝鋆

sentences.zh: 文慶，字孔修，費莫氏，滿州鑲紅旗人，兩廣總督永保之孫也。

translations.literal: Wen Qing, styled Kongxiu, of the Feimo clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner, was the grandson of Yongbao, Governor-General of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing, whose style was Kongxiu, belonged to the Feimo clan and came from the Manchu Bordered Red Banner; he was a grandson of Yongbao, governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of the Daoguang reign (1822), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 五遷至詹事。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted five times until he became Grand Mentor in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 歷通政使、左副都御史、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He successively served as Commissioner of the Transmission Office, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to hold the posts of transmission commissioner, left vice censor-in-chief, and grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授禮部侍郎，兼副都統。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently serving as Vice Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Daoguang (1832) he was made vice minister of rites and also appointed vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，總理孝慎皇后喪儀，會奏軍民薙發及停止宴會期限疏中，誤引「百姓如喪考妣，四海遏密八音」語，下諸臣嚴議。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he superintended the mourning rites for Empress Xiaoshen; in a joint memorial on the deadlines for shaving the head among soldiers and civilians and for suspending banquets, he mistakenly cited the phrase 'the people were as if mourning father and mother, and throughout the four seas the eight kinds of music were stopped,' and the matter was referred to the ministers for severe deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1833) he oversaw the mourning ceremonies for Empress Xiaoshen. In a joint memorial setting deadlines for military and civilian head-shaving and for halting banquets, he wrongly quoted the line that the people mourned as for father and mother and music was hushed throughout the realm; the case was sent down for strict review by the ministers.

sentences.zh: 宣宗以文慶翰林出身，隨聲附和，獨重譴，褫副都統，降三品頂戴。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor, considering that Wen Qing came from the Hanlin and had echoed others' views, singled him out for heavy censure, stripped him of the vice commandership, and reduced his hat knob to the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong held that Wen Qing, a Hanlin graduate who had simply echoed others, deserved punishment above the rest: he was stripped of his vice commandership and his hat knob was lowered to the third rank.

sentences.zh: 尋復之，歷吏部、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward this was restored; he successively served as Vice Minister of Personnel and of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored and went on to serve as vice minister of personnel and of revenue in turn.

sentences.zh: 十六年，偕尚書湯金釗赴陝西、四川按劾巡撫楊名颺、布政使李羲文，並下嚴議，尋复按名颺被訐事，褫其職。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, together with Minister Tang Jin-zhao he went to Shaanxi and Sichuan to investigate and impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Xiwen; both were referred for severe deliberation. Soon afterward, upon reinvestigating Yang Mingyang's impeachment case, Wen Qing was stripped of his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1836) he accompanied Minister Tang Jin-zhao to Shaanxi and Sichuan to investigate Governor Yang Mingyang and provincial administration commissioner Li Xiwen; both men were referred for severe punishment. When he later reopened the case of Yang's impeachment, Wen Qing himself was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 金釗留署陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: Tang Jin-zhao remained to act as Governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jin-zhao stayed behind as acting governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 文慶又按河南武陟知縣趙銘彝貪婪狀，劾褫職。

translations.literal: Wen Qing also investigated the greedy conduct of Zhao Mingyi, magistrate of Wuzhi in Henan, and impeached him, stripping him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing also investigated the corruption of Zhao Mingyi, magistrate of Wuzhi in Henan, and had him impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命在軍機大臣上學習行走，兼右翼總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was ordered to study and serve under the Grand Councilors, concurrently holding the post of Commander of the Right Wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1837) he was assigned to train under the Grand Council and also appointed commander of the right wing.

sentences.zh: 命赴熱河，偕都統耆英按歷任總管虧短庫款，褫職追繳。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Rehe, and together with Commander-in-Chief Qiying investigated successive superintendents' shortages in the treasury funds; they were stripped of office and made to pay restitution.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Rehe, where with Commander-in-Chief Qiying he investigated successive superintendents who had embezzled treasury funds; the culprits were dismissed and ordered to make restitution.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以查辦熱河虧空案內擬罪未晰，召問，奏對失實，下部議，罷直軍機。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, because the penalties proposed in the Rehe deficit case were unclear, he was summoned for questioning; his answers were untrue, the matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation, and he was removed from attendance at the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year (1839) the penalties in the Rehe deficit case were found unclear; summoned to explain, he gave false answers, the case went to the ministries, and he was removed from the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 二十年，典江南鄉試，以上下江中額有誤，又私攜湖南舉人熊少牧入闈閱卷，議褫職。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination; because the quotas for Upper and Lower Jiang were mistaken, and because he privately brought in the Hunan candidate Xiong Shaomu to grade papers inside the examination compound, dismissal from office was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1840) he served as chief examiner for the Jiangnan provincial examination. Errors in the Upper and Lower Jiang quotas, together with his having secretly brought the Hunan candidate Xiong Shaomu into the compound to grade papers, led to a proposal that he be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，予三等侍衛，充庫倫辦事大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was given the rank of third-class bodyguard and appointed Minister Resident at Khüree.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1842) he was made a third-class imperial bodyguard and appointed minister resident at Khüree.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，召授吏部侍郎、內務府大臣，連擢左都御史、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and Minister of the Imperial Household Department, and in rapid succession was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1843) he was recalled and made vice minister of personnel and minister of the Imperial Household Department, then quickly promoted to left censor-in-chief and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，命赴四川，偕總督、將軍按前任駐藏大臣孟保、鍾芳等濫提官物，劾罷之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was ordered to Sichuan, and together with the governor-general and the general investigated former Resident Ministers in Tibet Meng Bao, Zhong Fang, and others for abusively requisitioning official goods; they were impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (1845) he was sent to Sichuan, where with the governor-general and the general he investigated former Tibetan resident ministers Meng Bao, Zhong Fang, and others for illegally requisitioning official goods; they were impeached and removed.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，復命為軍機大臣，解內務府事務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was again appointed Grand Councilor and relieved of Imperial Household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1847) he was reappointed to the Grand Council and released from duties at the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 尋署陝甘總督，道經河南，命察賑務，劾玩誤之知縣四人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he acted as Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu; passing through Henan he was ordered to inspect relief work and impeached four magistrates for negligence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu. Passing through Henan on the way, he was ordered to inspect famine relief and impeached four magistrates for dereliction.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，召授吏部尚書，兼步軍統領、內務府大臣，罷直軍機處、兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, concurrently Commander of the Metropolitan Garrison, Minister of the Imperial Household, relieved of attendance at the Grand Council, and made concurrently Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1848) he was recalled as minister of personnel, also made commander of the metropolitan garrison and minister of the Imperial Household, removed from the Grand Council, and appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三十年，充內大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he served as Grand Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1850) he became a grand minister of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 薛執中者，甘肅河州人，以符咒惑眾。

translations.literal: Xue Zhizhong was a native of Hezhou in Gansu who deluded the masses with charms and incantations.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhizhong, a native of Hezhou in Gansu, won followers through charms and incantations.

sentences.zh: 至京師，藉術醫病，朝貴多與往來。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he used his arts to treat illness, and many court nobles associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: After he came to the capital he practiced healing by occult arts, and many high officials sought him out.

sentences.zh: 遂妄議時政，談休咎，行踪詭秘，為巡城御史曹楙堅捕治，中外大臣牽連被譴者眾。

translations.literal: He then presumptuously discussed current affairs and spoke of fortune and misfortune; his movements were secretive. The patrolling censor Cao Moujian arrested and punished him, and many ministers at court and in the provinces were implicated and censured.
translations.idiomatic: He then began to comment recklessly on politics and to speak of omens, while keeping his movements secret. Patrolling censor Cao Moujian arrested him, and a great many officials at court and in the provinces who had been connected with him were punished.

sentences.zh: 文慶曾延治病，文宗斥其身為步軍統領，不能立時捕究，有乖職守，褫職。

translations.literal: Wen Qing had once invited him to treat an illness. The Wenzong Emperor rebuked him, saying that as Commander of the Metropolitan Garrison he had failed to arrest and investigate at once, contrary to his duty, and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing had once called on him for treatment. Emperor Wenzong rebuked him: as commander of the metropolitan garrison he should have arrested the man at once, and for this breach of duty he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，予五品頂戴，辦理昌陵工程。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was given a fifth-rank hat knob and put in charge of works at Changling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng (1851) he was granted a fifth-rank hat knob and assigned to supervise construction at Changling.

sentences.zh: 二年，起授內閣學士，尋擢戶部尚書，復為內大臣、翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled and appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, soon promoted to Minister of Revenue, and again made Grand Minister and Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1852) he was recalled as a grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, soon promoted to minister of revenue, and again made a grand minister and chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 五年，復為軍機大臣、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again became Grand Councilor and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1855) he returned to the Grand Council and was made an associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 題孝靜皇后神主，加太子太保，拜文淵閣大學士，晉武英殿大學士，管理戶部，充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablet of Empress Xiaojing was inscribed, he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, placed in charge of the Ministry of Revenue, and made Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit tablet for Empress Xiaojing was inscribed, he was made grand guardian of the heir apparent, appointed grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, promoted to grand secretary of the Wuying Hall, put in charge of the Ministry of Revenue, and named chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 文慶醇謹持大體，宣宗、文宗知之深，屢躓屢起，眷倚不衰。

translations.literal: Wen Qing was pure, cautious, and upheld the larger principles; the Xuanzong and Wenzong emperors knew him deeply. Though he stumbled repeatedly he was repeatedly raised up, and imperial favor toward him never waned.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing was upright, cautious, and mindful of the larger interest. Emperors Xuanzong and Wenzong knew him well; though he fell from favor more than once, he was always restored, and their trust in him never faded.

sentences.zh: 時海內多故，粵匪猖熾，欽差大臣賽尚阿、訥爾經額先後以失律被譴。

translations.literal: At the time troubles were many within the realm; the Cantonese rebels raged fiercely, and the imperial commissioners Sai Shang'a and Ne'erjing'e were successively censured for breach of discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was beset by troubles, and the Cantonese rebels were raging. Imperial commissioners Sai Shang'a and Ne'erjing'e were censured in turn for military failures.

sentences.zh: 文慶言：「當重用漢臣，彼多從田間來，知民疾苦，熟諳情偽。

translations.literal: Wen Qing said: 'Han officials ought to be heavily employed; most of them come from the fields, know the people's hardships, and are thoroughly familiar with true and false circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing said, 'We should rely heavily on Han officials. Most of them rose from the countryside; they know the people's hardships and understand what is real and what is false.

sentences.zh: 豈若吾輩未出國門、懵然於大計者乎？

translations.literal: How can they compare with us, who have never left the capital gates and are ignorant of great strategy?'
translations.idiomatic: How can they compare with us, who have never left the capital and are blind to the larger plan?'

sentences.zh: 」常密請破除滿、漢畛域之見，不拘資格以用人。

translations.literal: ' He often secretly memorialized to break down Manchu–Han barriers in outlook and to employ men without being bound by formal qualifications.
translations.idiomatic: ' He often urged in secret memorials that the court set aside Manchu–Han divisions and appoint men without regard to rigid seniority rules.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓初任軍事，屢戰失利，忌者沮抑之。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan first took military command he suffered repeated defeats in battle, and jealous men obstructed and suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan first took up military command he met repeated defeats, and jealous rivals worked to hold him back.

sentences.zh: 文慶獨言國籓負時望，能殺賊，終當建非常之功。

translations.literal: Wen Qing alone said that Guofan enjoyed the esteem of the age, could kill rebels, and would in the end achieve extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing alone insisted that Guofan commanded public respect, could destroy the rebels, and would in the end win extraordinary distinction.

sentences.zh: 曾與胡林翼同典試，深知其才略，屢密薦，由貴州道員一歲之間擢至湖北巡撫，凡所奏請，無不從者。

translations.literal: He had once served with Hu Linyi as chief examiner and knew Hu's talent and strategy well; he repeatedly recommended him in secret. Within a single year Hu rose from circuit intendant in Guizhou to Governor of Hubei, and whatever Wen Qing memorialized was never refused.
translations.idiomatic: Having once served with Hu Linyi as chief examiner, he knew Hu's ability well and recommended him repeatedly in secret. Within a year Hu rose from Guizhou circuit intendant to governor of Hubei, and every request Wen Qing made on his behalf was granted.

sentences.zh: 又薦袁甲三、駱秉章之才，請久任勿他調，以觀厥成。

translations.literal: He also recommended the talents of Yuan Jiasan and Luo Bingzhang, asking that they be kept long in post without transfer so that their achievements might be seen.
translations.idiomatic: He also commended Yuan Jiasan and Luo Bingzhang and asked that they be left in office without transfer so their work could bear fruit.

sentences.zh: 在戶部，閻敬銘方為主事，當採用其議，非所司者亦諮之。

translations.literal: While at the Ministry of Revenue, Yan Jingming was then a section chief; Wen Qing held that his views ought to be adopted, and even matters outside his jurisdiction were referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Revenue, Yan Jingming was then only a section chief, yet Wen Qing adopted his advice and consulted him even on matters outside Yan's formal duties.

sentences.zh: 後卒得諸人力以戡定大難。

translations.literal: In the end, through the efforts of these men the great calamity was suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it was through such men that the great crisis was brought under control.

sentences.zh: 端華、肅順漸進用事，皆敬憚其嚴正焉。

translations.literal: Duanhua and Sushun gradually advanced in power; both respected and feared his severity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: As Duanhua and Sushun gradually came to power, both respected and feared his stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng (1856) he died.

sentences.zh: 遺疏言各省督撫如慶端、福濟、崇恩、瑛棨等，皆不能勝任，不早罷，恐誤封疆。

translations.literal: His final memorial stated that governors-general and governors such as Qingduan, Fu Ji, Chong'en, and Yingqi in the various provinces were all unfit for their posts; if they were not dismissed early, he feared the frontiers would be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: In his deathbed memorial he warned that governors such as Qingduan, Fu Ji, Chong'en, and Yingqi were unfit for their posts and that delay in removing them would endanger the provinces.

sentences.zh: 文宗深惜之，優詔賜卹，嘉其人品端粹，器量淵深，辦事精勤，通達治體，贈太保，賜金治喪。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor deeply regretted his loss, issued an excellent edict granting condolence payments, praised his upright character, profound capacity, diligent handling of affairs, and thorough grasp of governance, posthumously made him Grand Tutor, and granted gold for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong deeply mourned him, issued a generous edict of condolence, praised his integrity, depth of character, diligence, and mastery of statecraft, posthumously made him grand tutor, and granted funds for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 及親奠，見其遺孤幼穉，特詔加恩入祀賢良祠，命其子善聯俟及歲引見；

translations.literal: When the emperor personally offered sacrifice and saw his orphaned children still young, he specially issued an edict of added favor enrolling him in the Shrine of Worthies, and ordered his son Shanlian to await audience when he came of age;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor offered sacrifice in person and saw how young the orphans were, he specially ordered that Wen Qing be enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies and that his son Shanlian be presented at court when he came of age;

sentences.zh: 弟文玉，以罪遣戍，即釋回。

translations.literal: his younger brother Wenyu, who had been banished for a crime, was immediately released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Wenyu, who had been exiled for a crime, was immediately released and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 予諡文端。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wenduan ('Cultured and Upright').

sentences.zh: 善聯，官至福州將軍。

translations.literal: Shanlian rose to the post of General at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shanlian rose to become general at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 文祥，字博川，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正紅旗人，世居盛京。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang, styled bochuan, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, had his family seat in Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang, whose style was Bochuan, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and came from the Manchu Plain Red Banner; his family had long resided in Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年進士，授工部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was appointed a section chief in the Ministry of Works, and was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang (1845), entered the Ministry of Works as a section chief, and was promoted repeatedly until he became a director.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，京察，記名道府，因親老，乞留京職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, at the capital evaluation he was noted for circuit and prefectural posts, but because his parents were elderly he begged to remain in a capital post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng (1856), at the capital evaluation he was marked for provincial appointment, but with elderly parents at home he asked to remain in a capital post.

sentences.zh: 歷太僕寺少卿、詹事、內閣學士，署刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Grand Mentor, Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and acting Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, grand mentor, grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and acting vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 八年，命在軍機大臣上行走，授禮部侍郎，歷吏部、戶部、工部侍郎，兼副都統、左翼總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council, appointed Vice Minister of Rites, successively held the vice ministries of Personnel, Revenue, and Works, and concurrently served as Vice Commander-in-Chief and Commander of the Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng (1858) he joined the Grand Council and was made vice minister of rites, then held the vice ministries of personnel, revenue, and works in succession, while also serving as vice commander-in-chief and commander of the left wing.

sentences.zh: 十年，英法聯軍犯天津，僧格林沁密疏請幸熱河。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allied forces attacked Tianjin; Senggelinqin secretly memorialized asking that the court proceed to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1860) the Anglo-French allied armies threatened Tianjin, and Senggelinqin secretly urged the court to withdraw to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 文祥以搖動人心，有關大局，且塞外無險可扼，力持不可，偕廷臣言之，復請獨對；

translations.literal: Wen Xiang held that this would shake popular sentiment, bore on the larger situation, and that beyond the passes there were no defensible positions to hold; he strongly maintained it could not be done, spoke together with court ministers, and again requested a private audience;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang argued that such a move would unsettle the people, affect the whole strategic situation, and that beyond the passes there was no terrain that could be held; he strongly opposed it, spoke with other ministers, and again asked for a private audience;

sentences.zh: 退偕同直侍郎匡源、杜翰具疏請罷所調車馬，明詔宣示中外。

translations.literal: after retiring he joined his fellow councilor Vice Ministers Kuang Yuan and Du Han in submitting a memorial asking that the horses and carts already mobilized be dismissed, and that an explicit edict be proclaimed at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: afterward he joined fellow councilors Kuang Yuan and Du Han in a memorial asking that the mobilized transport be stood down and that an explicit edict reassure the court and the country.

sentences.zh: 八月，敵氛益熾，車駕遽行，命文祥署步軍統領，司留守。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the enemy threat grew fiercer and the imperial carriage departed hastily; Wen Xiang was ordered to act as Commander of the Metropolitan Garrison and oversee those who remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the enemy threat intensified and the court fled in haste; Wen Xiang was ordered to act as commander of the metropolitan garrison and oversee the capital in the emperor's absence.

sentences.zh: 從恭親王奕訢議和，出入敵營，於非分之求，侃侃直言，折之以理。

translations.literal: Following Prince Gong Yixin in negotiating peace, he went in and out of the enemy camp; toward improper demands he spoke forthrightly and refuted them with reason.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Gong Yixin in the peace negotiations, entering and leaving the enemy camp; when unreasonable demands were made, he spoke plainly and answered them with reason.

sentences.zh: 尋以步軍統領難兼顧，疏辭，改署正藍旗護軍統領。

translations.literal: Soon, because the metropolitan garrison command could not be attended to at the same time, he memorialized to resign and was changed to act as Commander of the Guards of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon finding the garrison command too much to combine with his other duties, he asked to be relieved and was made acting commander of the Plain Blue Banner guards.

sentences.zh: 十月，和議成，疏請回鑾，以定人心。

translations.literal: In the tenth month peace was concluded; he memorialized asking that the court return to the capital in order to settle popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month peace was concluded, and he memorialized urging the court to return to Beijing to steady public morale.

sentences.zh: 偕恭親王等通籌全局，疏上善後事宜，於是設立總理各國事務衙門，恭親王領之，滿、漢大臣數人，文祥任事最專。

translations.literal: Together with Prince Gong and others he planned the overall situation comprehensively and memorialized on post-settlement affairs; thereupon the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs was established, with Prince Gong at its head and several Manchu and Han ministers, among whom Wen Xiang bore the most concentrated responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Gong and others he planned the overall settlement and memorialized on postwar arrangements; the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs was then established under Prince Gong with several Manchu and Han ministers, and Wen Xiang shouldered the heaviest share of the work.

sentences.zh: 時和局甫定，發、捻猶熾，兵疲餉竭，近畿空虛。

translations.literal: At the time the peace settlement had only just been fixed; the Nian and Taiping rebels still raged, troops were weary and funds exhausted, and the capital region was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had only just been secured; the Nian and Taiping rebels were still active, the armies were exhausted and funds depleted, and the capital region lay largely undefended.

sentences.zh: 文祥密疏請選練八旗兵丁，添置槍砲，於是始立神機營，尋命管理營務。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang secretly memorialized asking to select and drill Eight Banner soldiers and add firearms and cannon; thereupon the Shenji Camp was first established, and soon he was ordered to manage camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang secretly urged that selected Eight Banner troops be drilled and equipped with firearms; the Shenji Camp was then established, and he was soon put in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 又疏言僧格林沁兵力單薄，勝保所部新募未經行陣。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Senggelinqin's forces were thin, and that the newly recruited troops under Sheng Bao had never seen battle.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Senggelinqin's forces were too few and that Sheng Bao's newly recruited men had never been tested in the field.

sentences.zh: 既恃僧格林沁保障畿輔，必得良將勁卒為贊助，薦副都統富明阿、總兵成明隸其軍；

translations.literal: Since the court relied on Senggelinqin to secure the capital region, good generals and strong soldiers had to assist him; he recommended Vice Commander Fuming'a and Brigadier Cheng Ming be placed under his command;
translations.idiomatic: Since the court relied on Senggelinqin to defend the capital region, he needed able generals and seasoned troops; Wen Xiang recommended Vice Commander Fuming'a and Brigadier Cheng Ming be attached to his command;

sentences.zh: 又薦江西九江道沈葆楨、湖北候補知縣劉蓉堪大用。

translations.literal: he also recommended Shen Baozhen, circuit intendant of Jiujiang in Jiangxi, and Liu Rong, expectant magistrate in Hubei, as men fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: he also commended Shen Baozhen, Jiujiang circuit intendant in Jiangxi, and Liu Rong, an expectant magistrate in Hubei, as men of outstanding ability.

sentences.zh: 疏上，並嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When the memorials were submitted, all were favorably accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted all of these recommendations.

sentences.zh: 十一年，文宗崩於熱河行在，穆宗即位，肅順等專政，文祥請解樞務，不許。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Wenzong Emperor died at the Rehe traveling palace; the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne; Sushun and others monopolized power; Wen Xiang asked to be relieved of Grand Council duties and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861) Emperor Wenzong died at Rehe; the new Emperor Muzong ascended the throne while Sushun and his faction held power. Wen Xiang asked to leave the Grand Council but was refused.

sentences.zh: 十月，回鑾，偕王大臣疏請兩宮皇太后垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the court returned to the capital; together with princes and ministers he memorialized asking that the two empress dowagers attend to government from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court returned to Beijing, and with the princes and senior ministers he memorialized that the two empress dowagers should rule from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，連擢左都御史、工部尚書，兼署兵部尚書，為內務府大臣，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was in rapid succession promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of Works, concurrently acting Minister of War, made Minister of the Imperial Household Department, and concurrently Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862) he was quickly promoted to left censor-in-chief and minister of works, also acting minister of war, minister of the Imperial Household Department, and commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二年，管理籓院事務。

translations.literal: In the second year he managed the affairs of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1863) he took charge of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 東南軍事以次戡定，江蘇、浙江省城克復，議加恩樞臣，固辭。

translations.literal: Southeastern military affairs were gradually brought under control; the provincial capitals of Jiangsu and Zhejiang were recovered; rewards for the Grand Councilors were proposed, but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: As southeastern campaigns were brought under control and the capitals of Jiangsu and Zhejiang were recovered, rewards for the Grand Council were proposed, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧复，首逆就殲，捷至，加太子太保，予侄凱肇員外郎。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiangning was recovered, the chief rebel was destroyed, and victory reports arrived; he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his nephew Kaizhao was made a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1864) Nanjing was recovered and the chief rebel destroyed; when the victory report arrived he was made grand guardian of the heir apparent and his nephew Kaizhao was granted a secretaryship in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，署戶部尚書，辭內務府大臣，允之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he acted as Minister of Revenue, resigned the post of Minister of the Imperial Household Department, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1865) he acted as minister of revenue, asked to be relieved of the Imperial Household post, and was allowed to step down.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，馬賊入喜峰口，命文祥率神機營兵防護東陵，督諸軍進剿，賊遁灤陽。

translations.literal: That autumn mounted bandits entered Xifeng Pass; Wen Xiang was ordered to lead Shenji Camp troops to guard the Eastern Tombs and supervise the various armies in pursuit; the bandits fled to Luanyang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn mounted bandits entered through Xifeng Pass. Wen Xiang was ordered to lead Shenji Camp troops to guard the Eastern Tombs and direct the pursuit; the bandits fled toward Luanyang.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「地方官豢賊釀患，請除積弊，清盜源。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'Local officials harbor bandits and breed trouble; I ask that accumulated abuses be removed and the sources of banditry cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'Local officials shelter bandits and breed disorder; accumulated abuses must be removed and the sources of banditry cut off.

sentences.zh: 馬賊巢穴多在奉天昌圖廳八面城、熱河八溝哈達等處。

translations.literal: The lairs of mounted bandits are mostly at Bamian Cheng in Changtu subprefecture in Fengtian, at Hadatu in Bagou in Rehe, and other such places.
translations.idiomatic: Their strongholds lie chiefly at Bamian Cheng in Changtu, Fengtian, at Hadatu in Bagou, Rehe, and similar places.

sentences.zh: 請購線偵察，調兵掩捕，庶絕根株。

translations.literal: I ask that informants be hired for reconnaissance and troops be moved for surprise capture, so that the roots may be cut off.'
translations.idiomatic: Informants should be hired for reconnaissance and troops sent to strike by surprise, so the problem can be uprooted entirely.'

sentences.zh: 」事定，回京。

translations.literal: ' When affairs were settled he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 文宗奉安山陵，賜其子熙聯員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor was interred at the mountain tomb, his son Xilian was granted a secretaryship in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong was laid to rest in the imperial tomb, his son Xilian was granted a secretaryship in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋以母病請假三月，回旗迎養。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because his mother was ill he asked for three months' leave and returned to his banner estate to bring her back for care.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, with his mother ill, he took three months' leave and returned to his banner estate to bring her home for care.

sentences.zh: 奉天馬賊方熾，命率神機營兵往剿，增調直隸洋槍隊出關，約東三盟蒙古王公由北路夾擊，破賊於錦州東井子。

translations.literal: Mounted bandits in Fengtian were then raging fiercely; he was ordered to lead Shenji Camp troops to suppress them, with additional detachments of foreign-rifle companies from Zhili sent beyond the passes; he arranged with the Mongol princes of the Eastern Three Leagues to strike from the north route and defeated the bandits at Dongjingzi near Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With mounted bandits raging in Fengtian, he was ordered to lead Shenji Camp troops against them, reinforced by foreign-rifle companies from Zhili sent beyond the passes; coordinating with Mongol princes of the Eastern Three Leagues from the north, he defeated the bandits at Dongjingzi near Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 諜知賊將劫奉天獄，約期攻城，兼程馳援，賊退踞城東南，圍撫順；

translations.literal: Spies learned that the bandits would raid the Fengtian prison and had set a date to attack the city; he rushed reinforcements day and night; the bandits withdrew to hold the southeast of the city and besieged Fushun;
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence showed the bandits planned to storm the Fengtian jail and attack the city on a set day; he marched reinforcements at forced pace; the bandits fell back to the southeast and besieged Fushun;

sentences.zh: 令總兵劉景芳夜擊破之，賊遁出邊。

translations.literal: he ordered Brigadier Liu Jingfang to attack by night and break them; the bandits fled beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered Brigadier Liu Jingfang to attack by night and rout them, and the bandits fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遣軍趨吉林，五年春，解長春廳圍，追賊至昌圖朝陽坡，分三路進擊，十數戰皆捷，擒斬三千餘。

translations.literal: He sent troops toward Jilin; in the spring of the fifth year he relieved the siege of Changchun subprefecture, pursued the bandits to Chaoyang Slope in Changtu, divided into three routes to attack, won victory in more than ten battles, and captured or killed more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He sent forces into Jilin; in the spring of the fifth year (1866) he lifted the siege of Changchun, pursued the bandits to Chaoyang Slope in Changtu, attacked along three routes, won more than ten engagements, and killed or captured over three thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊首馬傻子窮蹙乞降，磔之；

translations.literal: The bandit chief Ma Shazi, pressed to extremity, begged to surrender and was dismembered;
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader Ma Shazi, cornered, begged to surrender and was executed by dismemberment;

sentences.zh: 留兵餉授將軍都興阿，俾清餘孽。

translations.literal: he left troops and funds with General Duxing'a to enable him to clear the remaining rebels.
translations.idiomatic: he left troops and supplies with General Duxing'a to mop up the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 請蠲奉天地丁銀米，停鋪捐。

translations.literal: He asked that land-tax silver and grain in Fengtian be remitted and shop levies suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that land-tax payments in silver and grain for Fengtian be remitted and shop levies halted.

sentences.zh: 回京，調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Beijing he was transferred to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 文宗實錄成，賜子熙治員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Wenzong were completed, his son Xizhi was granted a secretaryship in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong were completed, his son Xizhi was granted a secretaryship in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁母憂，特賜諭祭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his mother and was specially granted an edict of sacrificial offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1869) he mourned his mother and was specially granted an imperial offering at the funeral.

sentences.zh: 百日假滿，病未出。

translations.literal: When the hundred days of leave ended he had not yet emerged because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When his hundred days of mourning leave ended he was still too ill to resume office.

sentences.zh: 天津教案起，力疾還朝。

translations.literal: When the Tianjin missionary case arose he forced himself to return to court despite illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianjin missionary incident broke out he forced himself back to court despite his illness.

sentences.zh: 十年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, as Minister of Personnel he became Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1871) he was made associate grand secretary while retaining the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Titren Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1872) he was appointed grand secretary of the Titren Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 文祥自同治初年偕恭親王同心輔政，總理各國事務，以一身負其責。

translations.literal: From the early Tongzhi years Wen Xiang assisted in government in concert with Prince Gong, directed foreign affairs, and bore the responsibility largely alone.
translations.idiomatic: From the early Tongzhi period Wen Xiang worked in close partnership with Prince Gong, directed foreign affairs, and carried most of the burden himself.

sentences.zh: 洋情譸幻，朝論紛紜，一以忠信持之，無諉卸。

translations.literal: Foreign affairs were shifting and deceptive, court opinion was divided and clamorous; he held to them throughout with loyalty and sincerity, without shirking.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign affairs were treacherous and court opinion divided, yet he met them with steadfast loyalty and sincerity and never shifted responsibility elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 洎穆宗親政，臚陳歷年洋務情形，因應機宜甚備，冀有啟悟。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor personally took charge of government, he set forth in detail the foreign-affairs situation over the years, with responses to circumstances thoroughly prepared, hoping for enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took personal charge of government, he laid out in full the course of foreign affairs over the years and the measures suited to each turn of events, hoping to awaken the emperor's understanding.

sentences.zh: 既而恭親王以阻圓明園工程忤旨斥罷，文祥涕泣，偕同列力諫，幾同譴。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Prince Gong, because he had opposed the Yuanmingyuan project and thereby defied the imperial will, was dismissed and rebuked; Wen Xiang wept and, together with his colleagues, pleaded forcefully, and nearly shared in the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Prince Gong was dismissed for defying the throne by blocking work on the Yuanmingyuan; Wen Xiang wept and joined his colleagues in forceful remonstrance, nearly sharing in the reprimand.

sentences.zh: 恭親王尋復職，而自屢遭挫折後，任事不能如初。

translations.literal: Prince Gong soon resumed office, but after suffering repeated setbacks he could no longer handle affairs as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong was soon restored to office, but after repeated setbacks he could no longer serve with his former energy.

sentences.zh: 文祥正色立朝，為中外所嚴憚，朝局賴以維持，不致驟變。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang stood in court with stern integrity and was deeply feared at home and abroad; the court situation relied on him to be maintained and did not change abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang confronted the court with stern integrity and was deeply respected at home and abroad; the political situation depended on him to hold steady and did not collapse suddenly.

sentences.zh: 十三年，病久不瘉，在告，會日本窺台灣，強出籌戰守。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, long ill without recovery, he was on leave; when Japan cast covetous eyes on Taiwan he forced himself out to plan defense and offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, still seriously ill and on leave, he forced himself back when Japan turned covetous eyes toward Taiwan and laid plans for defense.

sentences.zh: 疏請：「敕下戶部、內務府寬籌餉需，裁減浮用，停不急之工作，謀至急之海防，俾部臣、疆臣皆得專力圖維。

translations.literal: In a memorial he asked: 'May Your Majesty issue orders to the Board of Revenue and the Imperial Household Department to raise funds with latitude, cut wasteful expenditure, halt work that is not urgent, and plan coastal defense as the utmost urgency, so that ministers and frontier governors may all devote themselves entirely to maintaining order.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he asked: 'May Your Majesty order the Board of Revenue and the Imperial Household Department to raise funds generously, cut wasteful spending, halt non-urgent projects, and give top priority to coastal defense, so that central ministers and frontier governors may devote themselves wholly to keeping the realm secure.

sentences.zh: 皇上憂勤惕厲，斯內外臣工不敢蹈玩洩之習。

translations.literal: If the emperor is anxious and diligent and vigilant and strict, then officials within and without will not dare fall into habits of negligence and laxity.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor is vigilant and tireless in his duties, officials at court and on the frontier will not dare lapse into negligence and slackness.

sentences.zh: 否則狃以為安，不思變計，恐中外解體，人心動搖，其患有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: Otherwise, clinging to the thought that all is secure and failing to reconsider plans, I fear the realm will disintegrate at home and abroad and popular sentiment will waver—distress whose consequences cannot all be expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, clinging to a false sense of security and refusing to change course, the realm may unravel at home and abroad and popular loyalty may falter—disasters beyond reckoning.'

sentences.zh: 」言甚切至。

translations.literal: ' His words were extremely earnest and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: His words were piercing and urgent.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，穆宗崩，德宗繼統即位，晉武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: That winter Emperor Muzong died; Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne and Wen Xiang was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Emperor Muzong died; when Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, Wen Xiang was promoted to grand secretary of the Hall of Martial Splendor.

sentences.zh: 以久病請罷，溫詔慰留，解諸兼職，專任軍機大臣及總理各國事務。

translations.literal: Because of long illness he asked to resign; a warm edict comforted him and kept him in office, relieved him of various concurrent posts, and charged him solely as Grand Councilor and Superintendent of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign on account of prolonged illness; the throne responded with a warm edict urging him to stay, relieved him of his various concurrent posts, and kept him solely as grand councilor and superintendent of foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 時國家漸多故，文祥深憂之，密陳大計疏曰：「洋人為患中國，愈久愈深，而其窺伺中國之間，亦愈熟愈密。

translations.literal: As the state gradually faced more troubles, Wen Xiang was deeply troubled and in a secret memorial on the great plan said: 'The harm foreigners do to China grows deeper the longer it lasts, and their watching for openings in China grows ever more practiced and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm's troubles mounted, Wen Xiang grew deeply alarmed and submitted a secret memorial on grand strategy: 'Foreign powers harm China the longer they stay, and their search for openings in China grows ever more practiced and intimate.

sentences.zh: 從前屢戰屢和，迄無定局，因在事諸臣操縱未宜。

translations.literal: Formerly we fought and made peace again and again, yet never reached a settled outcome, because the officials handling affairs did not manage matters properly.
translations.idiomatic: We have fought and made peace again and again without ever securing a stable settlement, because those in charge of affairs handled matters poorly.

sentences.zh: 及庚申定約，設立衙門專司其事，以至於今，未見決裂。

translations.literal: Not until the Gengshen treaty was settled and a yamen was established to manage the matter exclusively has the situation, down to the present, been free of rupture.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the Gengshen treaty and the establishment of a dedicated office to manage relations has the situation held without rupture down to the present.

sentences.zh: 就事論事，固當相機盡心辦理，而揣洋人之用心，求馭外之大本，則不繫於此，所繫者在人心而已矣。

translations.literal: Judging the matter on its merits, one should indeed seize opportune moments and handle affairs wholeheartedly; yet in probing foreigners' intentions and seeking the great foundation for controlling them abroad, the key does not lie here—it lies in popular sentiment alone.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs should indeed be handled conscientiously as circumstances require; yet in reading foreign intentions and seeking the true foundation for managing external relations, the key lies not in diplomacy itself but in winning the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 溯自嘉慶年間，洋人漸形強悍，始而海島，繼而口岸，再及內地，蓄力厲精習機器，以待中國之間，一逞其欲。

translations.literal: Tracing back to the Jiaqing period, foreigners gradually showed themselves fierce and overbearing—first on the seas and islands, then at the treaty ports, then reaching the interior—storing strength, refining zeal, practicing machinery, waiting for China's openings to indulge their desires at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiaqing era foreigners have grown steadily more aggressive—first at sea, then at the treaty ports, then inland—building strength, mastering machinery, and waiting for an opening in China to satisfy their ambitions at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 道光年間，肆掠江、浙，自江寧換約以後，覬覦觀望。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period they plundered Jiangsu and Zhejiang; after the treaty exchange at Jiangning they looked on with covetous observation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang they ravaged Jiangsu and Zhejiang; after the treaty was exchanged at Nanjing they watched and waited with covetous eyes.

sentences.zh: 直至粵匪滋事，以為中國有此犯上作亂之事，人心不一，得其間矣。

translations.literal: Only when the Guangdong rebels stirred trouble did they decide that China had this crime of rebellion against superiors and disorder, that popular sentiment was not united—that they had found their opening.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping rebellion broke out they concluded that China was torn by rebellion and disunity—and that their opening had come.

sentences.zh: 於是其謀遂洩，闖入津門，雖經小挫，而其意愈堅，致有庚申之警。

translations.literal: Thereupon their schemes broke out: they stormed the gates of Tianjin; though they met minor setbacks, their intent grew firmer still, leading to the Gengshen crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Their designs then erupted: they forced their way to Tianjin; though briefly checked, their resolve hardened, culminating in the Gengshen crisis.

sentences.zh: 然其時勢局固危，民心未二，勤王之師雖非勁旅，而聞警偕來；

translations.literal: Yet though the situation was indeed perilous, popular sentiment was not divided; the armies rallying to the throne, though not crack troops, came together at the alarm;
translations.idiomatic: Though the situation was perilous, the people had not lost unity; armies rallying to the throne, though not elite forces, came together at the alarm;

sentences.zh: 奸細之徒雖被誘脅，而公憤同具，以是得受羈縻，成此和局。

translations.literal: traitorous agents though enticed and coerced, shared the same public indignation—by this they were kept on a leash and this peace settlement was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: and though spies were recruited, public outrage was shared—thus the foreigners were restrained and the present peace was secured.

sentences.zh: 十餘年來，仰賴皇太后、皇上勵精圖治，宵旰勤勞，無間隙之可尋；

translations.literal: Over more than ten years, relying on the Empress Dowager and the emperor exerting themselves to govern well, toiling from evening till dawn, with no gap to be found;
translations.idiomatic: For more than a decade the Empress Dowager and the emperor have governed with tireless devotion, leaving no opening to exploit;

sentences.zh: 在事諸臣始得遇事維持，未至啟釁，偶有乾求，尚能往返爭持，不至太甚，非洋務之順手，及在事者折沖之力，皆我皇太后、皇上朝乾夕惕，事事期符民隱，人心固結，有以折外族之心，而杜未形之患也。

translations.literal: officials in charge have been able to maintain affairs when matters arise and have not yet provoked conflict; when foreigners occasionally pressed demands, they could still argue back and forth and keep things from becoming too severe—it is not that foreign affairs have gone smoothly or that those in charge have been strong in negotiation; all is because our Empress Dowager and emperor are diligent morning and evening, in every matter seeking to accord with the people's hidden wishes, solidifying popular sentiment, thereby bending the hearts of foreign peoples and forestalling troubles not yet formed.
translations.idiomatic: Those handling affairs have kept matters from erupting into conflict; when foreigners have pressed demands, officials have still been able to push back and keep concessions from growing excessive. This is not because foreign affairs have gone smoothly or because negotiators have been unusually skilled, but because the Empress Dowager and the emperor labor tirelessly, align every policy with the people's wishes, and knit popular loyalty so tightly that it bends foreign ambition and forestalls dangers before they form.

sentences.zh: 然而各國火器技藝之講求益進，彼此相結之勢益固。

translations.literal: Yet the pursuit of firearms and technical skills among the various countries advances ever further, and the trend of mutual alliance grows ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each power presses ever further in firearms and technology, and their alliances grow ever tighter.

sentences.zh: 使臣久駐京師，聞我一政之當則憂，一或不當則喜，其探測愈精。

translations.literal: Envoys long resident in the capital worry when they hear one of our policies is right and rejoice when one is wrong—their probing grows ever more precise.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys long stationed in Beijing worry when a policy of ours is sound and rejoice when one goes awry—their scrutiny grows ever sharper.

sentences.zh: 俄人逼於西疆，法人計佔越南，緊接滇、粵，英人謀由印度入藏及蜀，蠢蠢欲動之勢，益不可遏。

translations.literal: Russians press on the western frontier; French designs aim to seize Vietnam, adjoining Yunnan and Guangdong; English schemes would enter Tibet and Sichuan from India—the stirrings of movement grow ever harder to check.
translations.idiomatic: Russia presses the western frontier; France aims at Vietnam on Yunnan's and Guangdong's borders; Britain schemes from India into Tibet and Sichuan—the stirrings of encroachment grow ever harder to contain.

sentences.zh: 所伺者中國之間耳，所惎者中國大本之未搖，而人心之難違耳。

translations.literal: What they watch for is only China's openings; what frustrates them is only that China's fundamental order has not yet wavered and popular sentiment is hard to go against.
translations.idiomatic: They watch only for openings in China; what checks them is that the foundations of the realm still hold and popular loyalty cannot easily be defied.

sentences.zh: 說者謂各國性近犬羊，未知政治，然其國中偶有動作，必由其國主付上議院議之，所謂謀及卿士也；

translations.literal: Some say the various countries are by nature like dogs and sheep and know nothing of governance; yet whenever they act at home, their sovereign must submit matters to the upper house for deliberation—what is called consulting the nobles and officials;
translations.idiomatic: Some say foreign nations are uncivilized by nature, yet whenever their governments act, the sovereign must submit proposals to the upper house for deliberation—what is called consulting the nobles and officials;

sentences.zh: 付下議院議之，所謂謀及庶人也。

translations.literal: submit them to the lower house for deliberation—what is called consulting the common people.
translations.idiomatic: and to the lower house—what is called consulting the common people.

sentences.zh: 議之可行則行，否則止，事事必合乎民情而後決然行之。

translations.literal: If deliberation finds a measure feasible it is carried out; if not, it is stopped—every matter must accord with popular sentiment before it is resolutely enacted.
translations.idiomatic: What passes is enacted; what fails is dropped—every measure must satisfy popular sentiment before it is firmly executed.

sentences.zh: 自治其國以此，其觀他國之廢興成敗亦以此。

translations.literal: They govern their own countries by this principle; they judge the rise, fall, success, and failure of other countries by this same principle.
translations.idiomatic: They govern themselves by this rule and judge the rise and fall of other nations by the same standard.

sentences.zh: 儻其國一切政治皆與民情相背，則各國始逞所欲為，取之恐後矣。

translations.literal: If all governance in a country runs counter to popular sentiment, then the various countries begin to indulge what they wish and race to seize it for fear of being late.
translations.idiomatic: When a country's policies run counter to popular sentiment, the powers at last indulge their ambitions and race to exploit it.

sentences.zh: 如土耳其、希臘等國，勢極弱小，而得以久存各大國之間者，其人心固也。

translations.literal: Countries such as Turkey and Greece, though extremely weak in power, have been able to endure long among the great powers because their popular sentiment is firm.
translations.idiomatic: Turkey, Greece, and the like are extremely weak yet have endured among the great powers because their peoples remain united.

sentences.zh: 強大如法國，而德國得以勝之者，以法王窮侈任性，負國債之多不可復計，雖日益額餉以要結兵心，而民心已去，始有以乘其間也。

translations.literal: France was powerful, yet Germany was able to defeat it because the French king was wastefully extravagant and willful, national debt beyond all reckoning; though he daily increased pay to win soldiers' hearts, popular sentiment had already departed—only then was there an opening to exploit.
translations.idiomatic: France was mighty, yet Germany prevailed because the French king indulged extravagance and caprice until the national debt was beyond reckoning; though he raised soldiers' pay to buy loyalty, the people had already turned away—and only then could others seize their chance.

sentences.zh: 夫人必自侮而後人侮之，物必先自腐而後蟲生焉。

translations.literal: A man must first degrade himself before others degrade him; a thing must first rot of itself before worms are born in it.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, a man invites contempt before others show it; corruption within precedes ruin from without.

sentences.zh: 理之所在，勢所必至。

translations.literal: Where principle lies, the trend must arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Where principle points, events must follow.

sentences.zh: 中國之有外國，猶人身之有疾病，病者必相證用藥，而培元氣為尤要。

translations.literal: China having foreign countries is like the human body having illness: the sick must match symptoms with medicine, yet nourishing the vital energy is especially important.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign pressures on China are like disease in the body: symptoms must be treated, but strengthening the vital core matters most.

sentences.zh: 外國無日不察我民心之向背，中國必求無事不愜於民心之是非。

translations.literal: Foreign countries daily scrutinize whether our popular sentiment inclines or turns away; China must ensure that in every matter it accords with what popular sentiment approves or rejects.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign powers daily watch whether our people stand with or against the throne; China must ensure that nothing it does violates what the people approve or condemn.

sentences.zh: 中國天澤分嚴，外國上議院、下議院之設，勢有難行，而義可採取。

translations.literal: In China the distinction between imperial grace and subjects is strict; establishing upper and lower houses as abroad would be hard to implement, yet the principle may be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: China's hierarchy between sovereign and subject is strict; establishing foreign-style upper and lower houses would be impracticable, yet the underlying principle can be adapted.

sentences.zh: 凡我用人行政，一舉一動，揆之至理，度之民情，非人心所共愜，則急止勿為；

translations.literal: In all our appointment of men and conduct of government, in every move and act, measuring against supreme principle and gauging popular sentiment—if it is not what hearts universally approve, then stop it urgently and do not proceed;
translations.idiomatic: In appointments and governance, every action should be tested against right principle and the people's mood; what hearts universally reject must be stopped at once;

sentences.zh: 事係人心所共快，則務期於成。

translations.literal: when a matter concerns what hearts universally rejoice in, then strive to bring it to completion.
translations.idiomatic: What hearts universally welcome must be pursued to completion.

sentences.zh: 崇節儉以裕帑需，遇事始能有備，納諫諍以開言路，下情藉以上通。

translations.literal: Uphold frugality to enlarge treasury needs so that when matters arise one may be prepared; accept remonstrance to open the channel of speech so that conditions below may thereby reach above.
translations.idiomatic: Uphold frugality to strengthen the treasury and meet emergencies; welcome remonstrance to open avenues of speech so that sentiment below may reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 總期人心永結，大本永固，當各外國環伺之時，而使之無一間可乘，庶彼謀不能即遂，而在我亦堪自立。

translations.literal: In general, expect popular sentiment to be forever knit and the great foundation forever firm; when the various foreign countries surround and watch, cause them to find not a single opening to exploit—then perchance their schemes cannot immediately succeed, and on our side we can also stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: The aim is to keep popular loyalty permanently knit and the foundations permanently firm, so that when foreign powers encircle and watch they find no opening to exploit, their designs cannot quickly succeed, and we can still stand on our own.

sentences.zh: 此為目前猶可及之計，亦為此時不能稍緩之圖。

translations.literal: This is a plan still within reach at present and a design that at this moment cannot be relaxed even slightly.
translations.idiomatic: This is a course still within reach now and a design that brooks no delay.

sentences.zh: 若待其間之既開，而欲為斡旋補苴之法，則和與戰俱不可恃。

translations.literal: If one waits until the opening has already appeared and then wishes to apply mediating and patching methods, then neither peace nor war can be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until the opening has already appeared and then seek to patch matters by diplomacy, neither peace nor war will avail us.

sentences.zh: 即使仍可苟安，而大局已不堪復問，則何如預防其間之為計也。

translations.literal: Even if one could still scrape by in safety, the overall situation would already be beyond further inquiry—how much better to plan by forestalling the opening.
translations.idiomatic: Even if temporary safety were still possible, the larger situation would already be beyond repair—how much better to forestall the opening while we still can.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年王茂廕奏陳夷務，謂：'海外諸國日起爭雄，自人視之，雖有中外之分，自天視之，殆無彼此之意。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Wang Maoyin memorialized on foreign affairs, saying: 'The overseas countries daily rise in rivalry; viewed by men, though there is distinction between China and abroad, viewed by Heaven, there is scarcely any sense of difference.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Wang Maoyin memorialized on foreign affairs, saying: 'The nations overseas compete ever more fiercely; in human eyes China and the West are divided, yet in Heaven's view there is scarcely any such distinction.

sentences.zh: '引書言'皇天無親，惟德是輔'，及大學平天下章三言得失，首人心、次天命、而終以君心為證。

translations.literal: ' He cited the Classic: 'Great Heaven has no favorites; it assists only the virtuous,' and the chapter on bringing peace to the realm in the Great Learning, which three times speaks of gain and loss—first popular sentiment, next the Mandate of Heaven, and finally the ruler's heart as proof.
translations.idiomatic: He quoted the scripture: 'Great Heaven has no favorites; it assists only the virtuous,' and the chapter on bringing peace to the realm in the Great Learning, which three times treats success and failure—first the people's hearts, then Heaven's mandate, and finally the ruler's own heart as the proof.

sentences.zh: 何其言之危且切歟！

translations.literal: How perilous and urgent his words were!
translations.idiomatic: How urgent and piercing his words were!

sentences.zh: 欲戢夷心，莫要於順民心，能順民心，斯足以承天心，固不待蓍蔡而昭然若睹耳。

translations.literal: To restrain the minds of foreigners, nothing is more essential than following popular sentiment; able to follow popular sentiment, one is sufficient to receive Heaven's mind—it need not await divination by milfoil or tortoise to be as clear as if seen.
translations.idiomatic: To check foreign ambition, nothing matters more than aligning with the people's hearts; align with the people and one aligns with Heaven itself—no divination is needed to see it plainly.

sentences.zh: 臣受恩最重，辦理洋務最久，實有見於洋人居心積慮之處，而現時尤為迫切緊要之關。

translations.literal: Your servant has received grace most heavily and handled foreign affairs longest; I truly see where foreigners harbor settled designs, and at present this is especially the urgent and critical juncture.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has received the deepest favor and managed foreign affairs longest; I have seen clearly where foreigners harbor long-nurtured designs, and the present moment is the most urgent and critical of all.

sentences.zh: 外國之求間在此，中國之彌間亦在此。

translations.literal: The foreign powers' seeking of openings lies here, and China's widening of openings also lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign powers look for openings here—and China widens those openings here as well.

sentences.zh: 在事諸臣，僅謀其末，我皇上實操其本。

translations.literal: The officials handling affairs only plan the branches; Our Emperor truly holds the root.
translations.idiomatic: The officials on the case scheme only at the branches, while Your Majesty truly holds the root.

sentences.zh: 用敢直陳，伏乞俯鑑芻言，將此摺時置左右，力求端本之治，以回隱患之萌。

translations.literal: I therefore venture to speak frankly, humbly begging Your Majesty to deign to consider my humble words, to keep this memorial at hand, and to strive for governance that sets right the root, so as to turn back the budding of hidden dangers.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore venture to speak plainly, humbly begging Your Majesty to consider these humble words, keep this memorial close at hand, and strive to govern from the root—so that hidden dangers may be checked before they sprout.

sentences.zh: 天下幸甚！

translations.literal: Great fortune for the realm!
translations.idiomatic: May the realm be greatly blessed!

sentences.zh: 先是，當台灣事平，文祥即偕恭親王議興海防，條上六事：曰練兵，曰簡器，曰造船，曰籌餉，曰用人，曰持久。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Taiwan affair was settled, Wen Xiang together with Prince Gong discussed establishing coastal defense and submitted six items in outline: training troops, selecting weapons, building ships, securing funds, selecting men, and persistence.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, once the Taiwan affair was settled, Wen Xiang and Prince Gong moved to strengthen coastal defense and submitted a six-point program: training troops, modernizing arms, building ships, securing funds, appointing the right men, and sustaining the effort over time.

sentences.zh: 各具條目，敕下中外大臣會議。

translations.literal: Each item was detailed, and an edict was issued ordering Chinese and foreign officials to confer.
translations.idiomatic: Each point was spelled out in detail, and an edict went out instructing officials at court and in the provinces to confer.

sentences.zh: 至光緒二年，疆臣覆奏，將復下廷議。

translations.literal: By the second year of Guangxu, frontier governors reported back, and the matter was about to be sent down again for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Guangxu, the frontier governors had reported back, and the matter was to be sent down once more for deliberation at court.

sentences.zh: 文祥已病不能出，自知且不起，乃密疏上曰：「馭外之端，為國家第一要務。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang was already ill and could not attend; knowing he would not recover, he submitted a secret memorial stating: 'Managing foreign relations is the nation's first priority.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang was already too ill to attend court; knowing he would not rise again, he submitted a secret memorial: 'Managing foreign affairs is the state's first priority.

sentences.zh: 現籌自強之計，為安危全局一大關鍵。

translations.literal: The present plan for self-strengthening is a great hinge on which the whole situation of security and danger turns.
translations.idiomatic: The self-strengthening program now under discussion is the great hinge on which the nation's security and peril turn.

sentences.zh: 臣衰病侵尋，心長智短，知不能永效犬馬以報主知。

translations.literal: My declining illness advances day by day; my heart is willing but my wits are short, and I know I cannot forever serve like a dog or horse to repay my sovereign's trust.
translations.idiomatic: My illness worsens by the day; my devotion outruns my judgment, and I know I cannot long serve as a loyal beast of burden to repay my sovereign's trust.

sentences.zh: 恐一旦填溝壑，則平生欲言未言之隱，無以上達宸聰，下資會議，何以對陛下？

translations.literal: I fear that once I fill a gully, what I have wished to say but have not yet said in private will not reach the imperial ear or aid deliberation below—how then could I face Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once I am gone, what I have long wished to say but have never voiced will never reach the throne or inform the deliberations below—how then could I face Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 此心耿耿，有非總理衙門原奏所能盡者，敢竭誠吐赤，為我皇上敬陳之。

translations.literal: This loyal heart harbors matters that the Zongli Yamen's original memorial cannot fully express; I dare exhaust my sincerity and speak plainly, respectfully stating them for my Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal though I am, there are matters the Zongli Yamen's original memorial cannot fully convey; I dare speak with all sincerity and lay them plainly before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 夫敵國外患，無代無之，然未有如今日之局之奇、患之深、為我敵者之多且狡也。

translations.literal: External troubles from enemy nations exist in every age, yet never has the situation been as extraordinary as today's, the danger as deep, or those who are our enemies as numerous and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Every age knows troubles from abroad, yet never has the case been as strange as today's, the peril as deep, or our adversaries as many and as cunning.

sentences.zh: 果因此患而衡慮困心，自立不敗，原足作我精神，惺我心志，厲我志氣，所謂生於憂患者正在於此。

translations.literal: If truly because of this danger one weighs and considers with a troubled heart and establishes oneself undefeated, that is altogether enough to animate our spirit, sharpen our mind, and stiffen our will—the very meaning of being born of worry and danger lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Handled rightly, this peril should stiffen our spirits, sharpen our minds, and rouse our resolve—it is precisely in such worry and danger that a people is forged.

sentences.zh: 至此而復因循洩沓；

translations.literal: Yet at this point to again procrastinate and be slack;
translations.idiomatic: Yet if at this juncture we again lapse into delay and slackness;

sentences.zh: 一聽諸數而莫為之籌，即偶一籌念而移時輒忘，或有名無實，大局將不堪設想，而其幾不待智者而決矣。

translations.literal: to leave everything to chance without planning; to plan briefly and then forget; or to have the name without the substance—the overall situation will become unthinkable, and the outcome needs no sage to decide.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave everything unplanned; if we plan in passing and then forget; or if we honor reforms in name while hollowing them out in fact—the country will face consequences too dreadful to contemplate, and the outcome scarcely requires a sage to foretell.

sentences.zh: 從前夷患之熾，由於中外之情相隔，和戰之見無定，疆吏又遇事粉飾，其情形不能上達於朝廷。

translations.literal: Previously the intensity of barbarian troubles arose because sentiment between court and regions was divided, views on peace and war unsettled, and frontier officials prettified matters when they arose, so that conditions could not reach the court.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, barbarian troubles grew fierce because court and provinces were estranged, no settled policy existed for peace or war, and frontier officials glossed over events as they arose, so that the true situation never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 坐是三失，而其患遂日久日深，無所底止。

translations.literal: Thus there were three losses from this passivity, and the trouble grew deeper day by day with no end.
translations.idiomatic: Three losses followed from this inertia, and the trouble deepened day by day without limit.

sentences.zh: 泰西各國官商一氣，政教並行，各商舶遠涉重洋，初至中華，處處受我侮抑，事事被我阻塞，其情鬱而不能不發者，勢也。

translations.literal: In Western nations, officials and merchants act as one, government and instruction proceed together; merchant ships cross vast oceans, and when they first arrived in China they were everywhere insulted and suppressed by us and blocked in every matter—their resentment, unable not to burst forth, was a matter of necessity.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western nations, officials and merchants move as one, and government and instruction advance together. When their merchant vessels first crossed the oceans to China, they met insult and obstruction at every turn; resentment built until it had to break out—that was the force of circumstances.

sentences.zh: 繼而見中國官之阻之者可以通，抑之者可以伸，必不可破之格，或取勝於兵力之相迫而卒無不破，此中國之為所輕而各國漸敢恣肆之機也。

translations.literal: Then they saw that Chinese officials who obstructed could be circumvented and those suppressed could prevail; barriers thought unbreakable sometimes yielded to military pressure and in the end none remained unbroken—this was the moment when China was held cheap and the various nations gradually dared to act willfully.
translations.idiomatic: Then they discovered that officials who blocked them could be circumvented and restraints that held them down could be overturned; barriers deemed unbreakable sometimes gave way before armed pressure until none truly held—this was how China came to be despised and foreign powers gradually dared to act with impunity.

sentences.zh: 迨至立約通商已有成議，而內無深知洋務之大臣，在外無究心撫馭之疆吏，一切奏牘之陳，類多敷衍諱飾。

translations.literal: By the time treaties for trade had been agreed, within there were no ministers who deeply understood foreign affairs, and outside no frontier officials who earnestly attended to governing and controlling; the memorials submitted were mostly perfunctory evasions.
translations.idiomatic: By the time treaties of trade were in place, the court had no minister who truly understood foreign affairs, and the provinces had no governor who earnestly mastered control of them; memorials filed were mostly evasive and cosmetic.

sentences.zh: 敵人方桀驁而稱為恭順，洋情方怨毒而號為懽忭，遂至激成事端，忽和忽戰；

translations.literal: When enemies were arrogant they were called deferential, and when foreign sentiment was resentful it was proclaimed joyful;
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant enemies were hailed as deferential, and bitter foreign grievances were reported as rejoicing;

sentences.zh: 甚且彼省之和局甫成，此省之戰事又起，賠款朝給，捷書暮陳。

translations.literal: So much so that when peace was just settled in one province, war broke out again in another; indemnities were paid in the morning and victory reports submitted in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: So that peace might be concluded in one province even as fighting erupted in another; indemnities were disbursed in the morning and victory dispatches filed by evening.

sentences.zh: 乘遭風之船以為勝仗，執送信之酋以為擒渠，果至兩軍相交，仍復一敗不可收拾。

translations.literal: Wind-stricken ships were counted as victories, and messengers bearing letters were seized and proclaimed captured chiefs; yet when the two armies truly met, defeat followed defeat beyond recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Ships wrecked by storms were counted as victories, and couriers bearing letters were seized and hailed as captured chiefs; yet when the armies truly clashed, defeat piled upon defeat until nothing could be salvaged.

sentences.zh: 於是夷情愈驕，約款愈肆，中外大臣皆視辦理洋務為畏途，而庚申釁起，幾至無可措手。

translations.literal: Thereupon foreign sentiment grew prouder and treaty terms more unrestrained; court and regional officials all regarded handling foreign affairs as a dreaded path, until the Gengshen incident arose and the situation nearly reached the point where nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign arrogance then swelled and treaty demands grew bolder; officials at court and in the provinces alike came to see foreign affairs as a road of dread, until the Gengshen crisis broke out and the state was nearly beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 自設立總理衙門，其事始有責成，情形漸能熟悉，在事諸臣亦無敢推諉。

translations.literal: Since the Zongli Yamen was established, affairs began to have assigned responsibility, conditions gradually became familiar, and officials handling the matter also no longer dared to shirk.
translations.idiomatic: Since the establishment of the Zongli Yamen, responsibility has been fixed, circumstances have gradually become familiar, and those charged with the work no longer dare to shirk it.

sentences.zh: 然其事非在事諸臣之事，而國家切要之事也。

translations.literal: Yet this is not merely the affair of the officials who handle it, but a matter of the utmost national importance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is not merely the business of the officials in charge—it is a matter of the highest national urgency.

sentences.zh: 既為國家切要之事，則凡為大清臣子者，無人不應一心謀畫，以維大局。

translations.literal: Since it is a matter of the utmost national importance, then all who are subjects of the Great Qing ought with one heart to plan and maintain the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: Being a matter of the highest national urgency, every subject of the Great Qing ought to plan with one heart to uphold the common weal.

sentences.zh: 況和局之本在自強，自強之要在武備，亦非總理衙門所能操其權盡其用也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the foundation of peace lies in self-strengthening, and the key to self-strengthening lies in military preparedness; this too is not something the Zongli Yamen alone can wield authority over and fully deploy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the foundation of peace lies in self-strengthening, and the key to self-strengthening lies in military preparedness—matters not wholly within the Zongli Yamen's power to command or fully employ.

sentences.zh: 使武備果有實際，則於外族要求之端，持之易力，在彼有顧忌，覦覬亦可潛消，事不盡屬總理衙門，而無事不息息相關也。

translations.literal: If military preparedness truly has substance, then in the demands of foreign peoples one can hold firm more easily; they will have scruples, and covetous designs can also be silently dissolved; the matter does not all belong to the Zongli Yamen, yet nothing is unrelated.
translations.idiomatic: If military preparedness is real, foreign demands can be resisted more firmly; rivals will hesitate, and designs of encroachment may dissolve quietly—not everything rests with the Zongli Yamen, yet nothing is unrelated to it.

sentences.zh: 乃十數年來，遇有重大之端，安危呼吸之際，事外諸臣以袖手為得計；

translations.literal: Yet over more than ten years, when major matters arise at moments when safety and danger hang by a breath, officials outside the matter take keeping hands off as the clever plan;
translations.idiomatic: Yet for more than a decade, whenever crisis has hung by a thread, officials not directly involved have treated standing aloof as the shrewd course;

sentences.zh: 事甫就緒，異議復生，或轉託於成事不說；

translations.literal: When matters are just settled, objections arise again, or blame is shifted with the saying that one should not discuss what is already done;
translations.idiomatic: Once a matter is settled, objections flare again, or blame is shifted with the excuse that finished business should not be reopened;

sentences.zh: 不問事之難易情形若何，一歸咎於任事之人。

translations.literal: Without asking whether the matter is difficult or what the circumstances are, one uniformly blames those who bear responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Without regard for difficulty or circumstance, responsibility is uniformly pinned on those who undertook the work.

sentences.zh: 是從前之誤以無專責而仔肩乏人，今日之事又以有專屬而藉口有自。

translations.literal: This is how formerly the error lay in having no dedicated responsibility and no one to bear the burden, while today the affair again provides an excuse because there is a dedicated office.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the fault was the lack of a dedicated charge and of anyone to shoulder the burden; today the fault is that a dedicated office exists—and with it, a ready excuse.

sentences.zh: 設在事諸臣亦同存此心，爭相諉謝，必至如唐臣杜甫詩中所謂'獨使至尊憂社稷'矣。

translations.literal: Suppose the officials handling the matter also harbored this mindset and mutually shirked blame—they would certainly reach what the Tang official Du Fu's poem calls 'only making the Son of Heaven worry for the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Were those in charge to share this mind and shirk one another, we would arrive at what Du Fu warned: 'Only the Son of Heaven bears the care of the realm.'

sentences.zh: 夫能戰始能守，能守始能和，宜人人知之。

translations.literal: One who can fight can then defend; one who can defend can then make peace—this all should know.
translations.idiomatic: Only he who can fight can defend; only he who can defend can make peace—everyone knows this.

sentences.zh: 今日之敵，非得其所長，斷難與抗，稍識時務者，亦詎勿知？

translations.literal: Today's enemies—unless one obtains what they excel at, it is absolutely hard to resist them; even those slightly acquainted with current affairs, how could they not know?
